J2.reason: Large net cross-trial variance plausibly reflects heterogeneous deterministic turnover costs, but gross cross-trial variance is a different estimator. The DSR reference defines variance over the tested Sharpe estimates; it does not establish that replacing net dispersion with gross dispersion calibrates a net10bp selection gate. A lower numerical hurdle is not evidence of calibration.
J2.requested_resolution: Before changing gates for new rules only, compare proposed estimator with the distribution of best net10bp fitness under identical costed null searches across relevant horizons/turnover. Predeclare estimator/version and effective date before new candidate evaluation; keep old ledger/configs/verdicts immutable. Show gross and net estimates side by side as diagnostics; no reruns of rejected rules.

J3.scope: Rounds2–4 use exactly19 completed null runs with identical search budget/settings, deterministic prespecified seeds, ties fail, best real fitness must exceed every null maximum; no validation-derived seeds/features; an eventual pass requires independently frozen BinanceJ1 before holdout proposal.
J3.limits: This is a per-round empirical screening gate (minimum rank p1/20), not a familywise5% claim over3future rounds. Existing search budget, validation gates, trial accounting and holdout approvals remain.

primary_reference.interpretation: Variance across tested Sharpe estimates and multiple trials enters the expected maximum. Gross-vs-net replacement is our modelling choice and needs calibration, not an explicit prescription of this paper.
